blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_n = 3n + 5\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh explicit formula (seedha qaida) hai: is mein \(a_n\) seedha position number \(n\) se milta hai, pichle term ki zaroorat nahi.
Humein pehle teen terms chahiye, yani \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Plan: formula mein \(n = 1\), phir \(n = 2\), phir \(n = 3\) rakhenge, aur rakhte waqt bracket zaroor lagayenge taake sign ki ghalti na ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = 3n + 5\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Explicit formula hai, is liye seedha \(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhenge. Har term doosre terms se azaad hai, is liye kisi bhi term ko pehle nikal sakte hain.

\(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhein
\[a_1 = 3(1) + 5 = 8\]
\[a_2 = 3(2) + 5 = 11\]
\[a_3 = 3(3) + 5 = 14\]
Kyun: Har dafa \(n\) ki jagah position number rakha. Order of operations yaad rakhein: pehle multiply (\(3 \times n\)), phir 5 jama. \(3(1) + 5\) ko \(3(6)\) samajhna ghalat hoga.

Tasdeeq
\[11 - 8 = 3,\quad 14 - 11 = 3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Formula \(3n + 5\) mein \(n\) ka coefficient 3 hai, is liye har agla term 3 zyada hona chahiye. Hamare terms mein farq 3 hi hai, to jawab sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_{n+1} = 4a_n - 7 \text{ and } a_1 = 3\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh recursive rule (pichle term se agla term banane ka qaida) hai. Is mein \(a_{n+1}\) yani agla term, \(a_n\) yani maujooda term se banta hai.
Pehla term \(a_1\) diya hua hai, wahi hamara shuru hai.
Plan: \(n = 1\) rakh kar \(a_2\) nikalenge, phir \(n = 2\) rakh kar \(a_3\). Beech ka term chhor kar aage nahi ja sakte.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_{n+1} = 4a_n - 7\), \(a_1 = 3\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Recursive rule hai: \(n = 1\) rakhne se formula \(a_2\) ko \(a_1\) se jorta hai, aur \(n = 2\) rakhne se \(a_3\) ko \(a_2\) se. Is liye terms tarteeb se, ek ke baad ek, nikalne parenge.

Pehla term
\[a_1 = 3\]
Kyun: Pehla term sawal mein diya hua hai; recursive rule ko shuru karne ke liye yeh zaroori hota hai.

\(a_2\) ke liye \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[a_2 = 4a_1 - 7\]
\[= 4(3) - 7 = 5\]
Kyun: \(n = 1\) rakhne se \(a_{1+1} = a_2\) aur right side par \(a_1\) aata hai. Qaida keh raha hai: maujooda term ko 4 se multiply karo, phir 7 minus karo. \(4 \times 3 = 12\), \(12 - 7 = 5\).

\(a_3\) ke liye \(n = 2\) rakhein
\[a_3 = 4a_2 - 7\]
\[= 4(5) - 7 = 13\]
Kyun: Ab maujooda term \(a_2 = 5\) hai. Isi liye \(a_3\) seedha nahi nikal sakta tha; pehle \(a_2\) chahiye tha.
Dhyan dein: \(a_3\) mein \(n = 3\) rakhna ghalat hai; formula \(n\) nahi, pichla term maangta hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_n = (n - 3)(n + 1)\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh explicit formula (seedha qaida) hai: is mein \(a_n\) seedha position number \(n\) se milta hai, pichle term ki zaroorat nahi.
Humein pehle teen terms chahiye, yani \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Plan: formula mein \(n = 1\), phir \(n = 2\), phir \(n = 3\) rakhenge, aur rakhte waqt bracket zaroor lagayenge taake sign ki ghalti na ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = (n - 3)(n + 1)\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Explicit formula hai, is liye seedha \(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhenge. Har term doosre terms se azaad hai, is liye kisi bhi term ko pehle nikal sakte hain.

\(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhein
\[a_1 = (1 - 3)(1 + 1)\]
\[= (-2)(2) = -4\]
\[a_2 = (2 - 3)(2 + 1)\]
\[= (-1)(3) = -3\]
\[a_3 = (3 - 3)(3 + 1)\]
\[= (0)(4) = 0\]
Kyun: Har bracket pehle alag hal kiya, phir dono ko multiply kiya. Sign ka qaida: negative \(\times\) positive = negative. \(n = 3\) par pehla bracket zero ho gaya, aur zero ko kisi bhi number se multiply karein to zero hi aata hai.
Dhyan dein: term zero bhi ho sakta hai; is mein koi ghalti nahi.

Expand kar ke tasdeeq
\[(n - 3)(n + 1) = n^2 - 2n - 3\]
\[n = 2:\ 4 - 4 - 3 = -3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Brackets khol kar formula \(n^2 - 2n - 3\) bana. Is mein \(n = 2\) rakha to bhi \(-3\) aaya. Do alag raston se ek hi jawab aana is baat ka saboot hai ke hisaab sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_1 = -1,\ a_{n+1} = \frac{3}{a_n + 2}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh recursive rule (pichle term se agla term banane ka qaida) hai. Is mein \(a_{n+1}\) yani agla term, \(a_n\) yani maujooda term se banta hai.
Pehla term \(a_1\) diya hua hai, wahi hamara shuru hai.
Plan: \(n = 1\) rakh kar \(a_2\) nikalenge, phir \(n = 2\) rakh kar \(a_3\). Beech ka term chhor kar aage nahi ja sakte.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_{n+1} = \frac{3}{a_n + 2}\), \(a_1 = -1\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Recursive rule hai: \(n = 1\) rakhne se formula \(a_2\) ko \(a_1\) se jorta hai, aur \(n = 2\) rakhne se \(a_3\) ko \(a_2\) se. Is liye terms tarteeb se, ek ke baad ek, nikalne parenge.

\(a_2\) ke liye \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[a_2 = \dfrac{3}{a_1 + 2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{-1 + 2} = \dfrac{3}{1} = 3\]
Kyun: Qaida: maujooda term mein 2 jama karo, phir 3 ko is jawab se divide karo. Pehle denominator (neeche wala hissa) hal kiya: \(-1 + 2 = 1\). Phir \(3 \div 1 = 3\).

\(a_3\) ke liye \(n = 2\) rakhein
\[a_3 = \dfrac{3}{a_2 + 2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{3 + 2} = \dfrac{3}{5}\]
Kyun: Ab maujooda term \(a_2 = 3\) hai, to denominator \(3 + 2 = 5\) bana. Jawab fraction \(\frac{3}{5}\) hai, isay decimal mein badalne ki zaroorat nahi.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{3}{a_n + 2}\) ka matlab poore \(a_n + 2\) se divide karna hai, \(\frac{3}{a_n} + 2\) nahi.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_n = 8 - \frac{20}{3 + n}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh explicit formula (seedha qaida) hai: is mein \(a_n\) seedha position number \(n\) se milta hai, pichle term ki zaroorat nahi.
Humein pehle teen terms chahiye, yani \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Plan: formula mein \(n = 1\), phir \(n = 2\), phir \(n = 3\) rakhenge, aur rakhte waqt bracket zaroor lagayenge taake sign ki ghalti na ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = 8 - \frac{20}{3 + n}\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Explicit formula hai, is liye seedha \(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhenge. Har term doosre terms se azaad hai, is liye kisi bhi term ko pehle nikal sakte hain.

\(n = 1\) aur \(n = 2\) rakhein
\[a_1 = 8 - \dfrac{20}{4} = 8 - 5 = 3\]
\[a_2 = 8 - \dfrac{20}{5} = 8 - 4 = 4\]
Kyun: Pehle fraction hal kiya: \(n = 1\) par neeche \(3 + 1 = 4\) aur \(20 \div 4 = 5\); \(n = 2\) par neeche 5 aur \(20 \div 5 = 4\). Phir 8 mein se minus kiya. Division pehle, minus baad mein.

\(n = 3\) rakhein
\[a_3 = 8 - \dfrac{20}{6} = 8 - \dfrac{10}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{24}{3} - \dfrac{10}{3} = \dfrac{14}{3}\]
Kyun: Is dafa 6 se 20 poora divide nahi hota, is liye fraction ko 2 se chhota kiya: \(\frac{10}{3}\). Fractions minus karne ke liye denominator ek jaisa chahiye, is liye 8 ko \(\frac{24}{3}\) likha (kyunke \(8 \times 3 = 24\)). Phir sirf upar wale minus: \(24 - 10 = 14\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (vi) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_1 = 1,\ a_{n+1} = (3a_n + 2)^2\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh recursive rule (pichle term se agla term banane ka qaida) hai. Is mein \(a_{n+1}\) yani agla term, \(a_n\) yani maujooda term se banta hai.
Pehla term \(a_1\) diya hua hai, wahi hamara shuru hai.
Plan: \(n = 1\) rakh kar \(a_2\) nikalenge, phir \(n = 2\) rakh kar \(a_3\). Beech ka term chhor kar aage nahi ja sakte.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_{n+1} = (3a_n + 2)^2\), \(a_1 = 1\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Recursive rule hai: \(n = 1\) rakhne se formula \(a_2\) ko \(a_1\) se jorta hai, aur \(n = 2\) rakhne se \(a_3\) ko \(a_2\) se. Is liye terms tarteeb se, ek ke baad ek, nikalne parenge.

\(a_2\) ke liye \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[a_2 = (3a_1 + 2)^2\]
\[= (3 + 2)^2 = 5^2 = 25\]
Kyun: Qaida: maujooda term ko 3 se multiply karo, 2 jama karo, aur phir poore jawab ka square lo. Bracket ke andar pehle: \(3(1) + 2 = 5\), phir \(5^2 = 25\).

\(a_3\) ke liye \(n = 2\) rakhein
\[a_3 = (3a_2 + 2)^2\]
\[= (75 + 2)^2 = 77^2\]
\[= (70 + 7)^2\]
\[= 4900 + 980 + 49\]
\[= 5929\]
Kyun: Ab \(a_2 = 25\), to bracket \(3(25) + 2 = 77\) bana. 77 ka square calculator ke baghair nikalne ke liye isay \(70 + 7\) likha aur \((x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2xy + y^2\) lagaya: \(4900 + 2(70)(7) + 49\).
Dhyan dein: \((3a_n + 2)^2\) mein square poore bracket ka hai; \(3a_n^2 + 2\) ya \(3a_n + 4\) likhna ghalat hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vii) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_n = (-2n)^2\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh explicit formula (seedha qaida) hai: is mein \(a_n\) seedha position number \(n\) se milta hai, pichle term ki zaroorat nahi.
Humein pehle teen terms chahiye, yani \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Plan: formula mein \(n = 1\), phir \(n = 2\), phir \(n = 3\) rakhenge, aur rakhte waqt bracket zaroor lagayenge taake sign ki ghalti na ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = (-2n)^2\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Explicit formula hai, is liye seedha \(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhenge. Har term doosre terms se azaad hai, is liye kisi bhi term ko pehle nikal sakte hain.

Formula ko saada karein
\[(-2n)^2 = (-2n)(-2n) = 4n^2\]
Kyun: \((-2n)^2\) ka matlab \((-2n) \times (-2n)\) hai. Minus \(\times\) minus = plus, aur \(2 \times 2 = 4\). Is liye formula asal mein \(4n^2\) hai aur sab terms positive honge.
Dhyan dein: \((-2n)^2\) aur \(-2n^2\) alag cheezein hain; bracket hone ki wajah se minus bhi square hota hai.

\(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhein
\[a_1 = 4(1)^2 = 4\]
\[a_2 = 4(2)^2 = 16\]
\[a_3 = 4(3)^2 = 36\]
Kyun: Pehle \(n\) ka square, phir 4 se multiply. Check: \(a_2 = (-4)^2 = 16\), asal formula se bhi wohi.

blocks.prompt: 2 (viii) Write down the first three terms of the sequence: \(a_n = (-1)^n\, 7n^2\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh explicit formula (seedha qaida) hai: is mein \(a_n\) seedha position number \(n\) se milta hai, pichle term ki zaroorat nahi.
Humein pehle teen terms chahiye, yani \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Plan: formula mein \(n = 1\), phir \(n = 2\), phir \(n = 3\) rakhenge, aur rakhte waqt bracket zaroor lagayenge taake sign ki ghalti na ho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = (-1)^n\, 7n^2\)
Humein find karna hai: pehle teen terms \(a_1, a_2, a_3\).
Tareeqa: Explicit formula hai, is liye seedha \(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhenge. Har term doosre terms se azaad hai, is liye kisi bhi term ko pehle nikal sakte hain.

\((-1)^n\) ko samjhein
\[(-1)^1 = -1,\ (-1)^2 = 1,\ (-1)^3 = -1\]
Kyun: \((-1)^n\) sirf sign ka faisla karta hai: odd (taaq) \(n\) par \(-1\) aur even (juft) \(n\) par \(+1\). Term ka size \(7n^2\) se aata hai. Is liye terms ka sign baari baari badlega: minus, plus, minus. Aisi sequence ko alternating (baari baari sign badalne wali) kehte hain.

\(n = 1, 2, 3\) rakhein
\[a_1 = (-1)(7)(1) = -7\]
\[a_2 = (+1)(7)(4) = 28\]
\[a_3 = (-1)(7)(9) = -63\]
Kyun: Har \(n\) ke liye sign ko \(7n^2\) se multiply kiya: \(7(1) = 7\), \(7(4) = 28\), \(7(9) = 63\). Phir \((-1)^n\) wala sign lagaya.
Dhyan dein: \(7n^2\) mein square sirf \(n\) par hai, 7 par nahi: \(7 \times 2^2 = 28\), \(14^2\) nahi.
